title: Ordered processing with a synchronous AWS Lambda target on Amazon EventBridge
description: Process events in order by invoking an AWS Lambda function synchronously from a FIFO subscriber on an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern shows how an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus (the eventsv2 API) processes events in order by invoking an AWS Lambda function synchronously (InvocationType REQUEST_RESPONSE) from a FIFO subscriber.

The publisher sends a sequence of OrderPlaced events that share one EventGroupId, each carrying a monotonically increasing sequence number. The FIFO subscriber delivers one event per batch and invokes the consumer Lambda synchronously, waiting for each event to be confirmed before delivering the next in the group. The consumer logs each sequence number as it processes, and the CloudWatch log shows the sequence handled in order, one at a time. Synchronous confirmation gives the reliability and back-pressure that teams used to get by adding an SQS queue between the bus and Lambda, so no queue is needed.

This deploys one EventBridge custom event bus, one FIFO subscriber configured for synchronous invocation, one Python 3.14 Lambda function, an SQS dead-letter queue (safety net), and the delivery role.
